thread:
Maya: Heads-up: our onboarding sample for the Go generator is misleading about streaming cancellation. The quickstart shows calling Generate(ctx, req) and then iter.Result(), but that blocks if the ctx is canceled during the initial handshake. Users hit this in smaller apps and it looks like a hang.

Ethan: Oof. We tried to keep the quickstart tiny, but didn’t cover the cancel case. Can you paste the exact snippet?

Maya: Very small: 
```go
iter, _ := client.Generate(ctx, req)
for tok := range iter.Stream() { fmt.Print(tok) }
fmt.Println(iter.Result()) // blocks if ctx canceled mid-handshake
```

Rui: We've seen this pattern in regressions. The iterator relies on an internal goroutine that completes the handshake and closes the stream. If ctx is canceled before that, Result() can wait forever.

Maya: Proposed fixes: (1) update quickstart to use a safe pattern that selects on ctx.Done() while consuming the stream; (2) add an Iterator.Close(context) in the SDK so callers can force cleanup; (3) mark Result() behavior in the streaming FAQ.

Ethan: I like keeping the quickstart defensive but simple. Suggest switching to the non-blocking consumption example: spawn a goroutine to forward tokens on a channel, then select on ctx.Done(). Small patch and easier to explain.

Rui: From SDK side, adding Close(ctx) is low-risk. We can implement it to close transport and cancel internal goroutines. Also make Result(ctx) accept a context (ResultWithCtx) and deprecate the blocking call.

Maya: I'll open a PR that updates quickstart, adds the sample, and files a SDK issue to add Close(ctx). Also adding a short note about reusing Generator across retries: create a new Generator if you expect aggressive cancel/retry loops.

CI-bot: Issue filed: #5123 "go-sdk: iterator blocks when ctx canceled during handshake". PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/256 (ci: linux/amd64 pass, darwin flake)

Ethan: Thanks Maya. Once the PR lands, let's update the streaming FAQ and the migration notes for 0.11.0.

Maya: Will do. Closing this thread after PR merges. Thanks! :sparkles:
